concepts.name: Scale-Out Compute
concepts.text: Splits jobs across nodes via horizontal scaling, partitioning, data locality, and fault tolerance (CAP trade-offs, MPP).

concepts.name: Apache Spark
concepts.tag: AWS Glue / Amazon EMR / Athena for Spark
concepts.text: Driver plans jobs; executors run tasks on partitions. Lazy transformations trigger on actions; wide ops cause shuffles.

concepts.name: Spark Bottlenecks
concepts.text: Minimize network shuffles (filter early, broadcast small tables), spread hot keys, and compact tiny files to 128 MB-1 GB.

concepts.name: Data Structures
concepts.text: B-trees power OLTP indexes; graphs model relationships and DAGs; hashes drive partitioning; Bloom filters skip data.

items.label: Plan (Driver)
items.text: Driver builds a DAG of lazy transformations and splits the job into stages at shuffle boundaries.

items.label: Execute Tasks
items.text: Executors run one task per partition; narrow ops (map, filter) process locally without moving data.

items.label: Shuffle & Act
items.text: Wide ops (join, groupBy) shuffle data across the network; actions (write, count) trigger execution.

table.heading: Key Data Structures
rows: Fast range and equality index lookups
Nodes and edges for deep relationships
Even key distribution and hash joins

tips: "Scale up" (bigger instance) rarely fixes a distributed bottleneck caused by data skew or many small files.
Neptune is the graph answer; avoid modeling deep relationship traversals in DynamoDB or RDS joins.
A DAG cannot contain cycles; orchestration retries come from retry policies, not cyclic edges.
Shuffles are the main cost in distributed SQL and Spark; Redshift distribution keys keep joined rows on the same slice.
